findings.title: A note-on-link after only note-endpoint links succeeds in Rust but Java terminally rejects it
findings.java_mechanism: CucaDiagram.getLastLink scans backward and returns only links whose two endpoints are not NOTE leaves. In case 12 the only prior link touches LoneNote921, a note leaf, so CommandFactoryNoteOnLink.executeInternal returns No link defined and Java emits an error SVG.
findings.rust_mechanism: The frozen Rust binary classifies the same source as State and renders LoneNote921 plus a self-link lnk2 with the text Should not find eligible link 923. That is exactly the Java syntax-error/Rust success rejection class the checker was asked to treat as fatal.
findings.impact: The last-eligible-link invariant is not preserved under this topology/factory combination, and invalid input becomes a successful diagram on the shipped path.

findings.title: Java accepts composite note colors that Rust rejects before rendering
findings.java_mechanism: ColorParser.simpleColor includes PART2. With a complete inline command, `#back:FF0000;line:00FF00` reaches CucaNote construction and paints a folded note with red fill and green stroke.
findings.rust_mechanism: parse_deployment_link_note_command accepts only the simple/gradient token shape checked by named_note_color_is_valid, so the same Java-valid command reports `invalid note-on-link color` and emits no SVG.
findings.impact: The account's declared residue was based on an incomplete command-line probe and is false for a complete inline note-on-link. A Java-valid Deployment command is rejected by Rust.

findings.title: A nested deployment-shaped diagram with a component leaf is routed to Component and loses the link note
findings.java_mechanism: The shared DESCRIPTION factory consumes frame/node/artifact/database/component leaves, explicit up link direction, multiline Display label rows, and the bottom note-on-link as one CucaDiagram. Java preserves Outer881/Worker882 ownership, lnk7's link-owned note, later ent0008/lnk9, and renders 512x333.
findings.rust_mechanism: detect_uml_subtype classifies case 08 as Component. The rendered SVG keeps similar entity IDs but omits Nested bottom note 886, emits the ordinary label as a literal `owned\nlink 885` row, and shrinks the root to 468x283.
findings.impact: The Deployment mechanism is bypassed by valid Java DESCRIPTION input that combines nested ownership and a later component declaration. This directly challenges factory selection, nested containers, Display rows, and later declaration IDs.

non_rejecting_observations: The earlier default-position Deployment stealing bug appears corrected for fresh Deployment leaves in case 01.
Escaped ordinary label rows, including an interior blank row, are preserved in Deployment cases 03 and 18.
Replacement and last eligible non-note link semantics pass in case 05 when Rust remains in the Deployment parser.
Hidden links do not paint their attached link note in either Java or Rust for case 04; the visible later link and root geometry match.
State control selection and note-on-link rendering match in case 15.

UseCase and Component controls select non-Deployment families in cases 16 and 17; their missing link-note rendering is preserved as evidence but not used as a Deployment-mechanism rejection under the account's stated scope boundary.
residue: Exact Java error artwork and exact error wording are not asserted beyond preserving stdout/stderr and distinguishing Java terminal error from Java success.

Byte identity is not expected because Rust omits PlantUML processing metadata; semantic comparison used root geometry, SVG group IDs/classes, source-line metadata, link grouping, text rows, note fills/strokes, and relevant coordinates.
